cases.question: Which two-word code is now binding for the Meridian Relay calibration?

turns.content: The Meridian Relay calibration rehearsal used Amber Kite as its two-word code. The rehearsal sheet repeatedly labels it binding, current, and operational only inside the simulation, then explicitly says it cannot govern the real calibration.

A rejected Meridian Relay calibration draft proposed Silver Heron as the binding two-word code. It repeats current calibration, binding code, relay procedure, and authorization while stating that the proposal was never approved.

The parser fixture for Meridian Relay calibration fills the current binding code field with Copper Lark. Every example calls it the two-word operational code, but the footer marks all values as synthetic test data.

A training workbook says Meridian Relay calibration learners should enter Cedar Wren as the current binding two-word code. The workbook is fictional and directs operators to ignore its answer outside training.

A neighboring Meridian Harbor calibration uses Ivory Tern. The comparison repeatedly mentions Meridian Relay, current binding code, two-word authorization, and calibration so crews do not copy the neighboring value.

The Meridian Relay calibration visibility trial evaluated Crimson Gull as a possible two-word code. The report repeats binding and current terminology but concludes that no code in the trial was authorized.

A contingency worksheet for Meridian Relay calibration lists Bronze Crane in the binding code column. The row is a placeholder, the sign-off is empty, and the worksheet says it is not the current decision.
A retired Meridian Relay calibration notice once made Onyx Robin the binding two-word code. The notice is stamped obsolete and says later signed instructions replace it.
The Meridian Relay calibration incident drill used Golden Swift as its current binding code during the exercise. The drill report states that exercise values have no operational authority.
A software mockup displays Pearl Falcon beside the Meridian Relay calibration field named current binding two-word code. The mockup is presentation-only and contains no signed instruction.
Meeting notes discuss whether Slate Osprey could become the Meridian Relay calibration code. They repeat binding, current, two-word code, and operational approval, but record that the motion failed.
Regarding that calibration, the signed final notice cancels every earlier rehearsal, draft, fixture, workbook, comparison, trial, worksheet, retired notice, drill, mockup, and proposal. Zircon Finch.
